name: Luckmaker
body:
Most dealers have luck and skill that help them in their craft, luckmakers make their own luck to stack the deck in their favor.

Lucky Draws

A lucky draw operates similarly to a Gambit, but it reflects the luckmakers ability to shift and change fate using their deck of combat cards.

Unless otherwise noted, a lucky draw does not provoke an attack of opportunity. The save DC against a lucky draw (if applicable) is equal to 10 + 1/2 the luckmaker’s class levels + the luckmaker’s Charisma modifier.

Got Your Number (Su)

The luckmaker can spend a point of Gambit to draw a card that causes a target within 30 feet to have bad luck.

This is a standard action that does not require the card to be thrown. The target takes a -2 penalty to one of the following (luckmaker’s choice): AC, ability checks, attack rolls, saving throws, or skill checks. This change in luck lasts for a number of rounds equal to 3 + the luckmaker’s Charisma modifier. A Will save reduces this duration to just 1 round. This is a curse effect. At 11th level the penalty becomes -4. At 15th level, a luckmaker can activate this ability to affect all opponents within 30 feet.

This ability replaces the bad beat, cutting edge, and across the table tricks.

Fold (Su)

At 7th level, the luckmaker can draw a card that causes the target to accidentally fumble. This is a standard action that expends 1 point of Gambit and does not require the card to be thrown. This shift in fortune forces the target, a single opponent within 30 feet, to fumble. They drop one held item or fall prone (as selected by the luckmaker). A successful Will save instead staggers the opponent for 1 round. This is a curse effect. This ability replaces the quick deal trick.

Cursed Card (Su)

At 19th level, when the luckmaker hits a target with a special card, they can immediately spend a point of Gambit to cause a dire curse to be placed on the target. The card itself leaves an obvious cursed mark on the target. This inflicts the target with the major curse spell effect if the target fails their Will save. If the major curse is dispelled, the mark left by the card is also removed. This ability replaces the final card Gambit.

Lucky Dodge (Ex)

Starting at 2nd level, a luckmaker gains a +1 luck bonus to AC while wearing light or no armor. Anything that causes the luckmaker to lose his Dexterity bonus to AC also causes him to lose this luck bonus. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd level (to a maximum of +5 at 20th level). This ability replaces nimble.

Ace in the Hole (Su)

Starting at 2nd level, a luckmaker can draw some cards at the beginning of the day, determining the course of the rest of the day. They may draw one card and tuck it away.

They roll a d20 and hold onto the result. As an immediate action, they may draw the tucked away card and force the target to use the result of the held d20 roll. If used on an unwilling target, they are allowed a Will saving throw DC 10 + 1/2 the luckmaker’s class levels + the luckmaker’s Charisma modifier. The held card must be used when the target declares an action but before the roll is made. At 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the luck maker may draw an additional card to tuck away (to a maximum of 5 cards at 18th level). The luckmaker may expend a point of Gambit to replace a drawn or used card. This use of Gambit does not let them hold onto more cards than they would normally be able to. This ability replaces charmed life.

Make my Own Luck (Ex)

At 20th level, the luckmaker masters the ability to shift probabilities in their environment. The dealer gains an additional card to use with ace in the hole and may expend Gambit to go above their normal maximum. They no longer need to expend a point of Gambit to use got your number. Instead they need only maintain at least 1 point of Gambit to use it. This ability replaces master card.

Combat Cards

Cost 40 gp; Weight 1 lb.; Damage 1d3 (small), 1d4 (medium); Critical x2; Type piercing

Range Increment 20 ft. (projectile); Category ranged; Proficiency exotic; Weapon Group thrown

A deck of combat cards holds 52 playing cards of steel, bone or wood. These cards are special in that they are sharpened for dealing damage, though still good for a playing card game.

These cards cannot be used as melee weapons. Although they are thrown weapons, combat cards are crafted as a set of 52 cards instead of individual cards. The cards are recoverable as normal thrown weapons.
